t: You're at Yale University Press, the university press of Yale University. It was founded in 1908 by George Parmly Day and Clarence Day, grandsons of Benjamin Day. It became a department of the university in 1961, though it remains financially and operationally independent. George Parmly Day, an American publisher, was its president from 1908 until 1944, so he led the press for its first thirty-six years and shaped what it became.
